Thanks. To check which programmes you may qualify for, I need a few more details:
1. How many people live in your household, including you? (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 or more)
2. Is there a married couple in the household? (no / yes)
3. Is anyone 65 or older? (no / yes)
4. Does anyone have a disability? (no / yes)
5. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none / $1-$10,000 / $10,000-$20,000 / $20,000-$30,000 / $30,000-$40,000 / $40,000-$50,000 / $50,000-$60,000 / $60,000-$80,000 / $80,000-$100,000 / $100,000-$150,000 / $150,000 or more)
6. Is anyone self-employed? (no / yes)
7. How much Social Security does the household get in a year? (none / $1-$10,000 / $10,000-$20,000 / $20,000-$30,000 / $30,000 or more)
8. Any other yearly income such as pensions, unemployment, interest, or child support? (none / $1-$5,000 / $5,000-$15,000 / $15,000 or more)
9. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000 / $2,000-$5,000 / $5,000-$20,000 / $20,000-$100,000 / $100,000 or more)
10. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (no / yes)
11. Is anyone a full-time college student? (no / yes)
reply: Two of us. Yes, my husband and I. Yes, that's right. No. Hard to say. I'm not sure. Hard to say. We don't have any of that. Somewhere between 350 thousand and 600 thousand. I don't really know. No.

summary: Arizona household: two married adults, no children, own their home, savings and investments about $350,000-$600,000, no Social Security or other income reported, no disability reported. Household work income and whether anyone is 65 or older could not be clearly confirmed, and employer health insurance status is unclear. Programmes ruled out on the known facts: WIC, TANF, CHIP, child tax credit, and free school meals (no children or pregnancy). SNAP and SSI are very likely out because of the savings level (SSI and SNAP asset limits apply, and SSI applies to seniors or people with disabilities). Not yet determinable: Medicaid (AHCCCS), ACA premium tax credit, and EITC, which depend on household income, employer coverage, and age. No programme is recommended without confirmed income, so a caseworker should confirm income, senior status, and employer insurance, then check Medicaid (AHCCCS), the ACA premium tax credit, and EITC.
